fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Entry Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Vehicle Parking Area; Detached Structure Complexity; Limited Side Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions of approach.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Mark or label the detached structure with its use so arriving responders can quickly identify what they are approaching.
• Keep the side access points unobstructed and clearly passable on foot.
• Remove any landscaping, planters, or decorative objects from the front entry area that would slow or block responder movement to the front door.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked vehicles along the path between the street and the front entry.
• Trim any shrubs or plantings along the walkway that narrow the usable path width.
• Post the property address at the street in numbers large enough to read from a moving vehicle at night.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Large Trees; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; None Visible
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the scattered tree clusters closest to the structure to increase open space between them.
• Remove shrubs growing directly beneath or adjacent to large trees to reduce the connection between ground-level plants and tree canopy.
• Keep the area between scattered shrub patches and any structures clear of additional dead or dry plant material.
• Trim lower branches on large trees near the structure to raise the canopy off the ground.
• Maintain the existing open terrain areas by preventing new shrub or tree seedling growth from filling in those spaces.
